Assume full AC. Use the canonical geometric Artin half twist in the oriented chart $(x,y,t)$, the canonical crossing sign $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, and the Seifert convention $\theta(u,v)=\operatorname{lk}(u^+,v)$. Let $F$ be the oriented braid Seifert surface consisting of two Seifert disks and the three crossing bands of the closure of $\sigma_1^3$. Label the bands in braid order $e_1,e_2,e_3$, oriented as edges from the first disk to the second. The cycle classes $a=e_1-e_2$ and $b=e_2-e_3$ form an integral basis. Order these two classes as $(u,v)$ so that $u\cdot_Fv=1$. Then
$$V_{(u,v)}=\begin{pmatrix}-1&1\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V+V^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\1&-2\end{pmatrix}.$$
In particular the signature is $-2$. The three pair-of-band annuli have core self-pairing $-1$, so they are positive Hopf bands when positive refers to the positively linked oriented boundary, rather than to core self-pairing $+1$.

actual_named_use: [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau|Knot Floer tau invariant]]
supplier_exact_statement:
Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

supplier_exact_statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

actual_named_use: [F2] The figure-eight matrix $V_F$ is a positive-push Seifert matrix; its skew part is the standard symplectic block. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection]]
supplier_exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.

For disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\theta_F(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The surface and basis are part of the data; this definition asserts no knot-only matrix invariant.

actual_named_use: [F3] Integral and field PTFA group rings have the compatible involution and fractions; a closed component's cyclic coefficient image gives nonsingularity when its fraction-field first homology vanishes. supplier_exact_statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be PTFA and let $k$ be either $\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field. The group ring $A=k[\Gamma]$ has no zero divisors, satisfies both Ore conditions, and has a fraction division ring $K$ in which every element is both a right and a left fraction of elements of $A$. The involution $\overline{\sum c_g g}=\sum c_g g^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive anti-automorphism of $K$.

Every intermediate unital ring $A\subseteq R\subseteq K$ has no zero divisors, satisfies both Ore conditions, and has this same $K$ as its fraction division ring. If $R$ is stable under the extended involution, that involution restricts to $R$ and descends to its additive quotient $K/R$. None of these assertions requires a choice principle.

4.3 Verify the trefoil grid in [F6] directly. Use row indices $0,1,2,3,4$ from bottom to top and column indices from left to right, as in [[def-grid-diagram-for-an-oriented-knot]], and draw the standard planar grid realization using the in-square mark-to-mark intervals. Following the grid orientation gives the single cycle
$$O_{0,4}\to X_{0,2}\to O_{2,2}\to X_{2,0}\to O_{4,0}\to X_{4,3}\to O_{1,3}\to X_{1,1}\to O_{3,1}\to X_{3,4}\to O_{0,4}.$$
The horizontal and vertical intervals meet away from their endpoints at exactly three crossings: $c_1=(\text{row }1,\text{column }2)$, $c_2=(\text{row }2,\text{column }1)$, and $c_3=(\text{row }3,\text{column }3)$. Traversing the component from $O_{0,4}$ encounters $c_1$ over, $c_2$ under, $c_3$ over, $c_1$ under, $c_2$ over, and $c_3$ under. At $c_1$ and $c_2$ the oriented projected tangents $(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$ are $((0,1),(-1,0))$; at $c_3$ they are $((0,-1),(1,0))$. Each determinant is $+1$ by [[def-planar-diagram-gauss-and-dowker-codes]]. Thus its signed oriented Gauss code is $1_O,2_U,3_O,1_U,2_O,3_U$ with crossing-sign vector $(+1,+1,+1)$. This code is also obtained by traversing the closure of the positive two-strand braid $\sigma_1^3$: its first braid strand encounters the three positive half twists over, under, over, and the returning strand encounters them under, over, under. The signed visit data determine the same crossing rotation and strand code, hence identify the face-permutation cycles. Retain the grid diagram's outer-face cycle and choose the corresponding face of the braid-closure diagram. To make this chosen face outer, compactify the projection plane to the oriented sphere $S^2$ and choose a point $q$ in that face, away from the diagram. An orientation-preserving rotation of $S^2$ sending $q$ to the projection point at infinity makes precisely this face outer. Realize the diagram lift in a product collar of the equatorial $S^2$ in $S^3$; the rotation extends by the same rotation on the first three coordinates and the identity on the normal coordinate. Its path of rotations is an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy of $S^3$ preserving the crossing heights and oriented strand data. The two resulting plane codes now have the same selected outer face, so [[thm-valid-code-reconstructs-the-declared-link-diagram]] identifies their diagrams up to planar isotopy. Thus the original grid and braid closure represent the same oriented knot even if their initially chosen planar outer faces differ. The braid closure lies on the standard unknotted torus with slope $2\alpha+3\beta$ (equivalently the swapped slope $3\alpha+2\beta$ under the orientation-preserving torus-coordinate swap), so it is $T(2,3)$ by [[def-coprime-torus-knot]]. The grid therefore represents the right-handed trefoil with its positive orientation, and its writhe is $+3$. [F6, F7, algebra]
supplier_exact_statement:
Let $P$ be the projection plane in an oriented $3$-sphere and let $n$ be the
unit viewing normal pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ so that $(u,v)$ is
a positive basis exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive ambient basis. A
**crossing code** has a
finite set $C$ of crossing labels and a finite set $D$ of **darts**, where a
dart is one directed half-edge incident to a crossing. A fixed-point-free
involution $\alpha:D\to D$ pairs the two ends of each edge: $\alpha^2=\mathrm{id}$
and $\alpha(d)\ne d$. A vertex map $v:D\to C$ records the crossing incident to
each dart. A **rotation system** is the permutation $\sigma$ whose cycles give
the clockwise order of darts at each crossing. Each crossing has four darts;
the two over-strand darts and the two under-strand darts are opposite in that
cyclic order. An arrow on each dart records whether its edge is directed into
or out of its incident crossing. The pairing $\alpha$ must join one incoming
end to one outgoing end. At a crossing, each opposite pair has one incoming
and one outgoing dart, so following an edge and then the opposite dart defines
the oriented link components. A code is **connected** when the graph with
vertices $C$ and edges the $\alpha$-pairs is connected.

The sign of an oriented crossing is $+1$ or $-1$ according as
$\det(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$ is positive or negative, where the two
tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. This item fixes
the local cyclic-order convention as follows. Starting with the outgoing
over-dart and reading counterclockwise, a positive crossing has order
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm out},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm in})$; a negative crossing has
order $(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm in},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm out})$. The stored crossing
sign and cyclic order must agree. This is the page's explicit sign convention.
It agrees with the current KT-03 supplier: reversing its positive
counterclockwise order from outgoing over gives the clockwise record
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm in},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm out})$.

For a nonempty connected crossing graph, let $V=|C|$, $E=|D|/2$, and let
$F$ be the number of cycles of the face permutation $\phi=\alpha\circ\sigma$.
A **spherical code** is a code satisfying $V-E+F=2$. A spherical code becomes a
**plane code** by distinguishing one face as the outer face and deleting a
point in that face from the sphere. The crossingless one-component code is a separate case: its Gauss data are one empty component word, its DT pairing and crossing-sign vector are empty at $c=0$, and its PD data are the single loop `Loop[1]`; every format also carries an orientation marker, `ccw` or `cw`, for the unit circle $S^1=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$ in the oriented plane, and the outer-face marker is `outside`. Thus the crossingless code records which direction orients its circle. It has no crossing graph or face-permutation test. Disconnected crossing graphs and disconnected crossingless links are outside this code class.

A **normalized planar-diagram code** with $c>0$ has crossing labels
$C=\{1,\ldots,c\}$ and four dart positions $0,1,2,3$ at each crossing, in
clockwise order beginning with the outgoing over-dart. The opposite pair
$(0,2)$ is over and $(1,3)$ is under. For sign $+1$, the clockwise record is
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm in},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm out})$; for sign $-1$ it is
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm out},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm in})$. Edge labels are assigned
by scanning crossings in increasing order and their four dart positions in
order, giving the next positive integer to the pair containing the first
not-yet-labelled dart. The outer face is recorded by its least dart in its
face cycle. These rules remove arbitrary edge-name and face-name choices;
different crossing labelings may still represent the same diagram. At $c=0$
a normalized code is the crossingless record with one of the two orientation
markers above.

A **Gauss code** for an oriented diagram records, in traversal order on each
oriented component, a signed crossing label: $+j$ means the component passes
over at crossing $j$, and $-j$ means it passes under. For a knot there is one
cyclic word; for a link there is one cyclic word per component. Each crossing
label must occur exactly twice in total, once positively and once negatively.
When $c>0$, every listed component word is nonempty; a separate crossingless
component is not part of this code class. The zero-crossing case is only the
one-component code specified above.
The code also carries a separate algebraic crossing-sign vector
$\varepsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$, one entry for each label. Choosing a basepoint
turns the knot's cyclic word into a based word; changing the basepoint
cyclically shifts the word, and relabeling crossings changes only their names.
The visit order, over/under signs, and crossing-sign vector determine the
crossing rotation system; it is realizable in the sphere only when the
resulting code is spherical. A plane Gauss code also carries an identifier of
one cycle of its face permutation to designate the outer face.

A **signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite code**, in this page's convention, encodes a
based oriented knot with $c$ crossings by numbering its $2c$ visits
$1,\ldots,2c$ in traversal order. For each odd visit $2j-1$, record the even
visit $2k$ paired with it as $d_j=+2k$ when the odd visit is over and
$d_j=-2k$ when it is under; also record the algebraic crossing sign
$\varepsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$ for crossing label $j$, the pair containing odd
visit $2j-1$. Its parity conditions are that
$|d_1|,\ldots,|d_c|$ are exactly the even numbers $2,4,\ldots,2c$, each once,
and each paired crossing has one over-visit and one under-visit. The separate
$\varepsilon_j$ records the crossing sign; signed DT conventions elsewhere
may encode signs differently. The associated cyclic traversal and crossing
signs determine a rotation system, which must pass the same spherical
realizability test. A plane DT code also carries an identifier of one cycle
of its face permutation to designate the outer face.

An **oriented planar-diagram code** labels each edge segment by an integer and
lists its two incident darts at crossing records. Each crossing record lists
its four directed edge ends in clockwise order, beginning with the outgoing
over-dart, and records which opposite pair is over, the orientation of each
strand, and the crossing sign. Every edge label occurs exactly twice, once as
an incoming end and once as an outgoing end. The code must satisfy the local
crossing-order rule above; its crossing graph must be connected when nonempty;
and its rotation system must satisfy $V-E+F=2$. The record also carries an
identifier of one cycle of its face permutation as the outer face. Thus an
arbitrary word in labels, even when each label occurs twice, is not declared
realizable until all incidence, orientation, crossing, connectedness, and
face-count tests pass.

supplier_exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.

For disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\theta_F(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The surface and basis are part of the data; this definition asserts no knot-only matrix invariant.

supplier_exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Supply an embedded admissible DOUBLY pointed diagram for an oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere, its compression disks and compatible Morse trajectory data, and a compact oriented Seifert surface $F$. Use the knot orientation from $w$ to $z$ in the alpha handlebody and from $z$ to $w$ in the beta handlebody. In positive genus let $x$ be a generator. In genus zero use the empty generator. There is an actual relative knot Spin-c lift $t_{w,z}(x)$ on the zero surgery $S^3_0(K)$, constructed with the following convention: on the knot exterior use the NEGATIVE of the compatible gradient after cancelling the index-one/index-two trajectories selected by $x$; across the zero-surgery solid torus use the zero-relative-Euler extension specified in the proof. Reversing this vector field convention would reverse its Alexander evaluation and is not silently permitted.

The integer
$$A_F(x)=\frac12\langle c_1(t_{w,z}(x)),[\widehat F]\rangle$$
is well defined, independent of the local extension and framing choices in that construction and of the choice of Seifert surface for the fixed oriented knot. For every actual Whitney class from $x$ to $y$,
$$A_F(x)-A_F(y)=n_z(\phi)-n_w(\phi).$$
The standard genus-zero unknot generator has value zero. The construction is carried by orientation-preserving isomorphisms of the supplied knot, surface and Morse data, and by a smooth mark-free attaching-curve isotopy with its followed generator. Swapping $w,z$ with the same underlying attaching systems gives $A_{z,w}(x)=-A_{w,z}(x)$; this is a statement about the actual Chern pairing, not a homological symmetry theorem. Its value can be computed as half the relative Euler number of the exterior perpendicular plane on $F\setminus N(K)$ with the explicit boundary frame in the proof; the solid-torus cap contributes zero.

Consequently this construction fixes the additive constant of the relative Alexander grading on every connected generator set. In an actual full filtered minus differential, including positive multiplicities at both basepoints, the term $U^{n_w(\phi)}y$ has Alexander level $A_F(x)-n_z(\phi)$. An exact finite matrix model of that diagram acquires its absolute grading by evaluating this Euler number at one generator and then using the relative differences. This last assertion does not claim that an uncalibrated numerical matrix or the relative grading alone already supplies that Euler evaluation. In particular, if an actual orientation-preserving diagram isomorphism exchanges the two marks, followed by a mark-free attaching-curve isotopy returning its generator to $y$ in the original diagram, then $A_F(x)=-A_F(y)$. If the relative calculation also gives $A_F(x)=A_F(y)$, both are zero. Arbitrary Heegaard-move comparison and a grid closed-form centering calculation are separate operations.

$$H_1(M;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu],\qquad H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\cong}H_1(V;\mathbb Z),\qquad H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}.$$
Put $\pi=\pi_1(V)$, take $n\ge0$, and supply classes $x_i,y_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n)}])$, $1\le i\le r$, satisfying $\lambda_n(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda_n(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. These are actual lifted half-pair data on the supplied manifold; existence of such a manifold or lifts is not asserted.

Let $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ for any prime $p$. Let $G$ be a discrete amenable group in $D(k)$ with $G^{(n+1)}=1$, and supply $\phi:\pi\to G$ such that $\phi(\mu)$ has infinite order. Use its based regular unitary local system and the finite-projective topological intersection convention. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(V,\phi)=0=\operatorname{sign}(V),$$
so its actual bounding signature defect is zero. This applies to the full supplied locally flat topological category as well as smooth manifolds; no finite CW type, smoothing, closed-manifold ordinary-versus-$L^2$ index equality or rho bordism-independence theorem is assumed. If a separately applicable bordism-independence result identifies a rho invariant with this bounding defect, that invariant is consequently zero.

supplier_exact_statement:
Assume AC. For every closed oriented smooth four-manifold $Z$ and every based homomorphism $\theta:\pi_1Z\to G$ to an arbitrary discrete group,
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(Z,\theta)=\operatorname{sign}(Z).$$
Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth three-manifold and $\phi:\pi_1M\to G$ any homomorphism. There exist an injective homomorphism $j:G\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ and a compact oriented smooth four-manifold $W$ with $\partial W=M$ and a homomorphism $\pi_1W\to\Gamma$ restricting to $j\phi$. For any such data put
$$\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_\Gamma(W)-\operatorname{sign}(W).$$
This number is independent of the smooth bound, its extending map and the injective target enlargement. The same value is obtained from $r$ copies of $M$ bounding a smooth $W$ by dividing its defect by $r>0$. Embedding the target group preserves the number. There is a finite constant $C_M$, depending only on the given smooth manifold $M$, such that
$$|\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi)|\le C_M$$
for all $G$ and $\phi$, including nononto homomorphisms and uncountable targets. For a disconnected compact $M$, use its finitely many components and the sum of these values, equivalently the free-product convention for its based fundamental groups. This is a signature-defect invariant among smooth bounds. No comparison with a nonsmooth TOP bound or an analytic eta definition is asserted.
